transcript:
Header: 2027-06-07 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Jordan Blake, Priya Khatri, Liam Ortiz (Redwood) — Alicia Chen, Miguel Torres, Sam Park, Noah Patel, Lina Gomez (NovaSearch)

Summary: Quick hosted API walkthrough focused on embeddings + rerank endpoints for search relevance use case. Covered integration options, latency/cost tradeoffs, and next steps for a 1-week pilot.

Topics: intro / current infra -> hosted embeddings -> reranking endpoint demo -> accuracy/latency tradeoffs -> security / SSO -> pilot next steps

00:00 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Hey everyone thanks for joining, you should all be muted on entry, I'm Jordan Blake from Redwood AE, with me is Priya our solutions engineer and Liam from product, Alicia, would you like to kick off with a quick intro?
00:12 Speaker 2 (Alicia): Yeah we can, thanks Jordan. I'm Alicia, Head of Search at NovaSearch, Miguel here runs our search infra, Sam is on the ML side. We're evaluating vector-based reranking to improve relevance, current stack: Elastic for indexing + a lightweight vector store prototype using Milvus, but it's getting expensive at scale. Primary asks are improved relevance, predictable latency under 150ms p95, and cost clarity.
00:38 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Awesome thanks. That tracks with what we saw in your intake form. Today's goal is a concise hosted demo of Redwood's embeddings + rerank API, show a sample pipeline for search re-rank, and surface latency/cost expectations. We'll leave time for security questions at the end.
00:51 Speaker 3 (Priya): Quick question on data residency and retention? Lina, do you want to share your constraints?
00:57 Speaker 4 (Lina): We need logs retained for 1 year for audit, sensitive PII must not be persisted in third-party stores, and SSO/SAML is required for admin console access. Also KMS integration for key management.
01:10 Speaker 3 (Priya): Noted — Redwood hosted supports SOC 2, encryption at rest, and customer KMS for Private deployments; hosted API can be configured with strict retention policies and we can show audit log configs in the console. We'll share the security whitepaper after the call.
01:28 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Ok demo time. Priya, take it away.
01:30 Speaker 3 (Priya): Cool. I'll share my screen — here's the Redwood Console home, quick nav: Models -> Hosted model catalog -> Embeddings endpoints. For NovaSearch you'll likely start with a dense vector embedder like redwood-embed-small or a 1536-dim open model we onboarded.
01:50 Speaker 3 (Priya): In this example we call the embeddings endpoint: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-1536","input":"How do I reset my password?"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' — that returns a 1536-d vector.
02:12 Speaker 3 (Priya): Then pipeline pattern: index raw docs in Elastic + store embeddings in your vector store OR use Redwood's embeddings index for quick prototyping. For rerank we show a single call to our rerank endpoint which accepts query, top-k candidates, and embeddings or candidate ids. Example payload I demo: {"query":"reset password account","candidates":[{"id":"doc123","text":"How to change password"}, ...]}
02:36 Speaker 2 (Alicia): Quick clarifying — do you require us to host vectors elsewhere or can you do the end-to-end?
02:44 Speaker 3 (Priya): Both. For hosted API you can store vectors in your system or use Redwood's managed embeddings index. For production we see teams keep vectors internal for control, but Redwood's managed index is convenient for pilots.
03:01 Speaker 5 (Miguel): What does the rerank model actually run? Is it a cross-encoder? How do you manage latency if it's cross-attention?
03:09 Speaker 3 (Priya): Great question — our rerank service offers a few strategies. We can do a fast vector-sim prefilter (approx nearest neighbors) then run a lightweight cross-encoder reranker for top 10-30 candidates. Kernel-level optimizations and batching reduce per-call latency; for hosted we aim for sub-200ms for rerank at small k, though exact numbers depend on sequence length and model choice. We'll share benchmark numbers.
03:33 Speaker 1 (Jordan): I'll flag that for the cost math. We typically recommend a two-stage approach to balance cost/latency.
03:40 Speaker 3 (Priya): Now I'll run a live example. Sending a demo query through the hosted API — initiating request... (typing) — returned results in ~120ms p95 for this local demo across sample docs. You'll see scores and reranked list printed.
04:05 Speaker 6 (Sam): The output shows confidence numbers, can we map that into our ranking signals?
04:11 Speaker 3 (Priya): Yes you can take the rerank scores and combine them with your BM25 or other signals — Redwood returns structured scores and feature breakdowns. Also function-calling style structured outputs are supported if you want consistent schema.
04:28 Speaker 5 (Miguel): How do you handle embeddings versioning? If we re-run embeddings with new model, how to avoid drift?
04:36 Speaker 3 (Priya): We support model versioning and backfills; the console shows per-model embedding hashes and we provide tooling to do rolling re-embeds with minimal downtime. We also have quality-monitoring in Optimize that can run prompt/embedding evals against a test set to detect drift.
04:55 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Let's touch on costs — Priya can explain the per-token and per-embedding unit breakdown.
05:02 Speaker 3 (Priya): For hosted embeddings we bill per-embedding call unit; rerank has per-request compute and optional per-token if we do autoregressive rerank. For your estimated 100M queries/month, the two-stage approach with small cross-encoder on top-k of 10 provides the best balance. We'll produce a sample spreadsheet that shows committed capacity and burst pricing.
05:26 Speaker 5 (Miguel): Is there a way to have reserved capacity for predictable p95 SLAs?
05:31 Speaker 3 (Priya): Yes — Redwood Dedicated offers reserved GPU pools and SLA-backed latency/uptime; for hosted we offer committed throughput contracts for larger customers which reduces variability. We'll include a pricing row for committed capacity in the follow-up.
05:46 Speaker 7 (Noah): For integration complexity, what's the time to prototype?
05:51 Speaker 3 (Priya): For a sandbox/proof of concept, teams usually have something working within a week using hosted embeddings + rerank with a small dataset. The pilot we suggest is 1 week with Redwood creating test API keys and a small benchmark run.
06:04 Speaker 4 (Lina): Security again — audit logs, retention and SSO. Does the hosted console support SAML SSO for admin?
06:12 Speaker 3 (Priya): Yes SAML/SSO for console admins and RBAC for keys; for hosted API keys we can restrict scopes and provide token rotation guidance. Audit logs are available and retention can be configured; for stricter controls customers opt for Private deployment with KMS integration.
06:30 Speaker 2 (Alicia): On results quality, can you share prior examples of improvements vs BM25?
06:36 Speaker 3 (Priya): We have benchmark slides — typical gains are 10-40% MAP/Recall lifts depending on dataset and prompt engineering. I'll drop the benchmark deck link in the notes.
06:50 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Quick check — any regulatory/regional constraints?
06:54 Speaker 2 (Alicia): We have EU customers, prefer data residency in EU for GDPR; initial pilot can be US but production must be in EU region.
07:05 Speaker 3 (Priya): Noted. Hosted supports region selection and we can provision EU region endpoints; for strict data residency Private is an option.
07:14 Speaker 5 (Miguel): On the API side, any SDKs?
07:17 Speaker 3 (Priya): We have Python, Node, and Java SDKs with examples for embeddings + rerank flows. Also a Postman collection.
07:28 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Let's do a short live run of a misranking case and how we'd tune prompts/embeddings. Priya?
07:33 Speaker 3 (Priya): Sure. I ran a sample where BM25 had doc A first but reranker moved doc B to top because of semantic match. I show the feature breakdown — you can see embedding similarity + token overlap signals. We then tweak candidate retrieval k and prompt template which improves precision@1.
08:02 Speaker 6 (Sam): Can we bring our own fine-tuned reranker model? We have an in-house cross-encoder trained on click data.
08:10 Speaker 3 (Priya): You can bring-your-own-model for reranking in Dedicated and Private; for hosted there are restrictions on custom model hosting but we can explore BYO-model via our dedicated offering or managed custom model service.
08:25 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Ok wrapping up demo portion. Any outstanding tech blockers?
08:30 Speaker 5 (Miguel): Need to validate p95 <=150ms on EU region with expected doc lengths and top-k=10. Also want an estimate for cost at 100M queries/month.
08:41 Speaker 3 (Priya): We'll run a sample benchmark on EU region using your sample dataset and share results.
08:45 Speaker 4 (Lina): Also confirm that PII can be redacted or excluded from logs and that we can configure retention to zero for content.
08:52 Speaker 3 (Priya): Yes redaction and retention policies can be applied; we'll document these configs.
08:58 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Great, let's recap next steps. Jordan, can you run through?
09:02 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Action items recap: Jordan will send pricing and committed capacity options; Priya will share benchmark script, sample dataset and deck; Priya will also provision a test API key for NovaSearch; Lina will send security checklist; Alicia will confirm pilot participants. We'll aim to kick off pilot week of 2027-06-21.
09:22 Speaker 2 (Alicia): Sounds good. One more quick question — is there a place in the console to see cost per route or per API key so we can attribute spend?
09:30 Speaker 3 (Priya): Yes Console -> Observability -> Cost allocation shows per-route and per-key breakdowns; you can set alerts for spend thresholds. We'll include screenshots.
09:44 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the recording and docs.
09:48 Speaker 2 (Alicia): Thank you!
09:49 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Bye all.

References shared during call: https://redwood.ai/decks/hosted-embeddings-rerank.pdf, benchmark spreadsheet (link shared in chat), sample Postman collection link.

End of transcript.
